title: Union home plaque and Jacques Pepitone's WWL speech
summary: Hirsch recalls the union home and a missing plaque, then tells of union president Pepitone's gaffe at the WWL 50,000-watt dedication.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: We had a lot of things, we had a lot of things down there that we found up there. Yeah. And we wanted to have them sort of remember a rebellion room. Dave, I don't want anything like that. In fact, Winstein, I even, I was president of the Home Association, I still am. Not that it means anything. But, I told Dave, I said, we ought to get these, we ought to have a bronze plaque who built this, our building now and this and the officers. I don't want to, it's just, if we put that up, is there any mistakes in the building? He's the guy that made the mistakes. He doesn't want anybody to know that he made the mistakes. So, we never did get a bronze. You saw the plaque that I have in the backyard, huh?

That was over in Mandeville. And, I had to go to a meeting one day and I was supposed to take my wife to the racetrack, which I didn't take. And I went to the meeting and she went down there and she says, well, for missing the racetrack, there's one thing that I wanted. Because we had sold at home over in Mandeville, where it was. Come out here and show it to you. All right. He had a very beautiful interpretation of the English language when he said, hello, musician, a union.
You know, musicians. This is Pepiton.

The dedication of WWL when they went 50,000 watts. They had the mayor of the city and they had this guy and this guy and this guy and this guy. And from Loyola University and now, this is Jacques Pepiton, who is the president and business agent of the local musician's union. He gets on. I got evening a ladies and a gentleman. He says, it's a great pleasure to be here with you folks tonight. He said, and I want to wish you WWL a lot of luck because they need it. He said, now, WWL is a good station because they hire a union musicians. He said, now you take that WSMB. They're no good. He's up there, man. He's telling who's good and who's not good because they're in time. Who has what and what. That was the thing that broke up the whole parade. I was wondering about Toe KT.
